title: Lifecycle contract and task dispositions
objective: Establish the minimal typed lifecycle contract that makes partial sprint outcomes truthful and keeps scopes open for subsequent planning.

phases.title: Contract characterization
phases.objective: Turn the current implicit lifecycle behavior into a compatibility-aware contract.

tasks.title: Map lifecycle owners and compatibility boundaries
tasks.description: Inventory every reader and writer affected by task state, close checkpoints, handoff routing, scope status, Doctor, Integrity, adapters, and fixtures; record the smallest compatible contract change.
tasks.context: The current state conflates closing the final roadmap sprint with completing a scope. This task must produce a source-grounded compatibility map before schema changes.
acceptance_criteria: Every lifecycle field changed by this scope has one identified writer and all identified readers.
Historical checkpoint and retirement compatibility behavior is explicit and does not require rewriting immutable bytes.
The selected disposition representation does not add a new CLI root unless existing writers are proven insufficient.

evidence.summary: Mapped every lifecycle field this scope may change to a single writer and its readers, and recorded the additive task.disposition contract (extend record-evidence; no new CLI root).

checked_criteria: Every lifecycle field changed by this scope has one identified writer and all identified readers.
Historical checkpoint and retirement compatibility behavior is explicit and does not require rewriting immutable bytes.
The selected disposition representation does not add a new CLI root unless existing writers are proven insufficient.

tasks.title: Add the typed task-disposition contract
tasks.description: Implement and validate the minimal disposition structure for unfinished tasks, including reason, actor, time, and required continuation references for deferred or superseded work.
tasks.context: A disposition is not a success verdict. The schema must preserve done+pass as verified completion and reject unknown, incomplete, or contradictory terminal records.
acceptance_criteria: Deferred, blocked, superseded, and cancelled work can be represented without changing it to done or pass.
Invalid disposition kinds, blank reasons, and invalid continuation targets fail without writes.
Existing valid v4 state remains readable under an explicit compatibility policy.

evidence.summary: Added optional task.disposition (deferred|blocked|superseded|cancelled) with schema validation and record-evidence --disposition/--reason/--target. Invalid kinds, blank reasons, and bad continuation targets fail without writes. Existing v4 tasks remain valid when the field is omitted.

checked_criteria: Deferred, blocked, superseded, and cancelled work can be represented without changing it to done or pass.
Invalid disposition kinds, blank reasons, and invalid continuation targets fail without writes.
Existing valid v4 state remains readable under an explicit compatibility policy.

phases.title: Truthful close semantics
phases.objective: Make close-sprint capture partial work truthfully without terminalizing the scope.

tasks.title: Make close-sprint derive truthful outcomes
tasks.description: Require every unfinished task to have a valid disposition, derive and persist the sprint outcome, and include dispositions in dry-run, checkpoint, ledger, snapshot, and narrative output.
tasks.context: The close transaction remains lossless and idempotent. It must never claim shipped from incomplete or disposed work.
acceptance_criteria: A partial close cannot proceed until every unfinished task has an explicit disposition.
The close dry-run and immutable checkpoint expose each unfinished task and its disposition.
A completed outcome remains available only when all tasks are done with passing verdicts.

evidence.summary: Made close-sprint reject undisposed unfinished work, derive a truthful partial/shipped outcome, preserve dispositions in close artifacts, and keep retries bound to the exact frozen semantic inputs.

checked_criteria: A partial close cannot proceed until every unfinished task has an explicit disposition.
The close dry-run and immutable checkpoint expose each unfinished task and its disposition.
A completed outcome remains available only when all tasks are done with passing verdicts.

tasks.title: Decouple final sprint close from scope completion
tasks.description: Change status and handoff derivation so every non-retired scope remains open and routable after sprint close, including when the original roadmap has no remaining entries.
tasks.context: Retirement stays human-gated and terminal. Scope completion is intentionally not inferred in this increment.
acceptance_criteria: Closing the last originally planned sprint does not set nextAction to done or scope status to completed.
The normal plan command can materialize a later sprint without recovery or manual state editing.
Retirement remains the only existing terminal path and retains its current approval behavior.

evidence.summary: Final P2 certification: every non-retired close remains routable to planning; close handoff and Integrity fixtures now assert the same post-close planning status.

checked_criteria: Closing the last originally planned sprint does not set nextAction to done or scope status to completed.
The normal plan command can materialize a later sprint without recovery or manual state editing.
Retirement remains the only existing terminal path and retains its current approval behavior.

phases.title: Observability and regression contract
phases.objective: Align reports and focused tests with the new lawful lifecycle.

tasks.title: Expose dispositions in status and fresh-context routing
tasks.description: Report unresolved disposed work and the open-scope planning route without hiding independent ready work or presenting a false completion state.
tasks.context: The CLI and instruction layer must agree; no agent should be told to stop because a roadmap estimate ended.
acceptance_criteria: Status distinguishes verified completion from deferred, blocked, superseded, and cancelled work.
Context-pack routes an open post-close scope to planning.
Close guidance no longer equates a final roadmap sprint with a completed scope.

evidence.summary: Status and fresh-context routing expose dispositions and keep open post-close scopes routed to planning: TaskSummary now reports verified completion separately from deferred/blocked/superseded/cancelled dispositions; context-pack derives scope status via deriveScopeStatus (matching kyro status) so an open post-close scope reads planning instead of a stale stored field; close-sprint.md guidance no longer equates exhausting the original roadmap with a completed scope.

checked_criteria: Status distinguishes verified completion from deferred, blocked, superseded, and cancelled work.
Context-pack routes an open post-close scope to planning.
Close guidance no longer equates a final roadmap sprint with a completed scope.

tasks.title: Add load-bearing lifecycle regressions
tasks.description: Extend existing lifecycle gates with adversarial partial-close, final-roadmap, invalid-disposition, historical, and retirement cases; avoid creating a duplicate test harness.
tasks.context: The tests must falsify the prior automatic-done behavior and prove archives remain immutable and retirement distinct.
acceptance_criteria: Reverting the no-auto-complete derivation breaks a focused regression.
Invalid or missing dispositions break a focused regression without writes.
A partial final-roadmap close can plan another sprint while retirement remains terminal.

evidence.summary: Extended existing lifecycle gates with adversarial load-bearing regressions: check-close-handoff adds partial final-roadmap close (persists partial outcome, scope stays planning/plan_sprint, never done) and undisposed-task close refusal without writes; check-status adds deriveScopeStatus mutation guard (roadmap exhaustion without done handoff must derive planning, not completed) and CLI task-summary disposition/verified distinction; check-plan adds S3 (plan materializes a later sprint after an exhausted roadmap close through the normal route).

checked_criteria: Reverting the no-auto-complete derivation breaks a focused regression.
Invalid or missing dispositions break a focused regression without writes.
A partial final-roadmap close can plan another sprint while retirement remains terminal.

emergentTasks.title: Unify next-executable-task routing to exclude disposed tasks
emergentTasks.description: Fix the T1.2 disposition regression: a disposed task (deferred/superseded/cancelled, which keep status pending) was re-selected by review's status-only next-task picker and reappeared in the executable routes. Extract one shared pure nextExecutableTaskId selector (pending|in_progress, no disposition of any kind, blocked excluded) and use it in BOTH record-evidence and review so the two writers cannot drift. Closing semantics unchanged: a disposed task never becomes done and never enables close_sprint by itself; when no executable task remains the handoff stays execute_task with nextTaskId null.
emergentTasks.context: QA flagged a Major failure of T1.2: record-evidence excluded dispositions but review.ts did not, so review re-selected a disposed pending task. The corrective task is tracked additively; T1.2's recorded evidence and review stay historical.
acceptance_criteria: A shared nextExecutableTaskId selector lives in core/status.ts and is used by both record-evidence and review.
Disposing T1.1 (deferred/superseded/cancelled), approving T1.2, never routes the handoff back to T1.1.
A pending task without disposition is still selected; a disposed emergent task is not.
A no-disposition sprint keeps prior routing and a blocked task without disposition still routes to review_task.
check-record-evidence.mjs covers these cases end-to-end and npm run check passes.

evidence.summary: Unified the next-executable-task routing on a single pure selector in core/status.ts (nextExecutableTaskId) that considers only pending|in_progress, excludes every disposition kind, and keeps blocking excluded. record-evidence and review now share it, removing the two divergent criteria that let review re-select a disposed pending task. Additionally, review now rejects ANY disposed task up front (DISPOSED_TASK_NOT_REVIEWABLE) for both pass and fail, before plan construction, so no review path can reopen disposed work. Closing semantics preserved: a disposed task never becomes done, never enables close_sprint by itself, and with no executable tasks left the handoff stays execute_task with nextTaskId null.

checked_criteria: A shared nextExecutableTaskId selector lives in core/status.ts and is used by both record-evidence and review.
Disposing T1.1 (deferred/superseded/cancelled), approving T1.2, never routes the handoff back to T1.1.
A pending task without disposition is still selected; a disposed emergent task is not.
A no-disposition sprint keeps prior routing and a blocked task without disposition still routes to review_task.
check-record-evidence.mjs covers these cases end-to-end and npm run check passes.

emergentTasks.title: Correct disposed-task review remedy
emergentTasks.description: Replace the inaccurate clarify instruction in DISPOSED_TASK_NOT_REVIEWABLE with only currently legal continuation paths, so an agent is not sent to a command that cannot reopen disposed work.
acceptance_criteria: The disposed-task review remedy does not present clarify as a re-open path.
The remedy directs active-sprint work to kyro add-emergent and labels any true reopen operation as future/explicit.

evidence.summary: Corrected the disposed-task review remedy so it names only an active-sprint replacement path and a future explicit reopen operation.

checked_criteria: The disposed-task review remedy does not present clarify as a re-open path.
The remedy directs active-sprint work to kyro add-emergent and labels any true reopen operation as future/explicit.

emergentTasks.title: Add post-close context-pack E2E regression
emergentTasks.description: Prove through the compiled CLI that a scope whose final roadmap sprint closes partially is still reported as planning by context-pack and routes to plan_sprint.
emergentTasks.context: Close derives planning; context-pack must expose the same canonical lifecycle state.
acceptance_criteria: A partial final-roadmap close followed by context-pack --json reports status planning and nextAction plan_sprint.
The regression fails if context-pack reads a stale stored completed status instead of deriveScopeStatus.

evidence.summary: Added an end-to-end post-close context-pack regression that injects a stale completed field after a partial final-roadmap close and requires canonical planning/plan_sprint output.

checked_criteria: A partial final-roadmap close followed by context-pack --json reports status planning and nextAction plan_sprint.
The regression fails if context-pack reads a stale stored completed status instead of deriveScopeStatus.

definitionOfDone: The lifecycle contract has source-grounded compatibility evidence.
All Sprint 1 tasks have passing reviewed evidence.
Focused lifecycle regressions and npm run check pass.
Doctor scoped to adaptive-sprint-lifecycle passes after the implementation.
